title: Fiducia as faith’s formal act — or only its inseparable effect (Garissol)
source_text: XLIII. Praeterea plurimi Scholae Reformatae Doctores non solum, ut supra vidimus, fiduciam numerant inter actus fidei; sed eam esse volunt actum fidei proprium formalem, atque specificum, & partem ejus primariam. Alii tamen videntur in diversa esse sententia; docent enim fiduciam esse quidem partum & effectum fidei, non tamen fidei actum proprie dictum. Haec est inter alios sententia Garissolii, dum viveret, in Academia Montis Albani Professoris. Si quaeras, inquit, Annon Fides sit fiducia? Respondeo, Fiduciam quidem indissolubili nexu cum fide cohaerere; non tamen, si proprie loquamur, esse fidem, sed effectum, necessario quodam partu, a fide pullulantem. In Explicatione Catecheseos Religionis Christianae, ad Sectionem decimam octavam.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover most Doctors of the Reformed School not only, as we have seen above, number trust among the acts of faith; but will have it to be the proper formal and specific act of faith, and its primary part. Yet others seem to be of a diverse opinion; for they teach that trust is indeed the offspring and effect of faith, yet not an act of faith properly so called. This among others is the opinion of Garissol, while he lived Professor in the Academy of Montauban. If you ask, he says, Is Faith then trust? I answer, Trust indeed coheres with faith by an indissoluble bond; yet, if we speak properly, it is not faith, but an effect, by a certain necessary birth, sprouting from faith. In the Explanation of the Catechesis of the Christian Religion, at the eighteenth Section.
pass_b_english: Most Reformed: fiducia = proper formal/specific act and primary part of faith.
Others: fiducia is faith’s offspring/effect — not faith’s act properly.
Garissol (Montauban): fiducia coheres inseparably with faith but is effect, not faith itself.
